vsm2.20:61.1:
Having attributed them thus, he again attributes the three characteristics to that same materiality by means of moving
forward and moving backward, looking toward and looking away, bending and stretching, thus:
vsm2.20:61.2: The materiality occurring in the moving forward ceases there without reaching the moving backward;
vsm2.20:61.3:
the materiality occurring in the moving backward … the looking toward; the materiality occurring in the looking
toward … the looking away; the materiality occurring in the looking away … the bending;
vsm2.20:61.4:
the materiality occurring in the bending ceases there without reaching the stretching:
therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self (cf. M-a I 260).
vsm2.20:62.1:
Next he divides a single footstep into six parts as “lifting up,” “shifting forward,”
“shifting sideways,” “lowering down,” “placing down,” and “fixing down.”
vsm2.20:63.1: Herein, lifting up is raising the foot from the ground.
vsm2.20:63.2: Shifting forward is shifting it to the front.
vsm2.20:63.3: Shifting sideways is moving the foot to one side or the other in seeing a thorn, stump, snake, and so on.
vsm2.20:63.4: Lowering down is letting the foot down.
vsm2.20:63.5: Placing down is putting the foot on the ground.
vsm2.20:63.6: Fixing down is pressing the foot on the ground while the other foot is being lifted up.
vsm2.20:64.1:
Herein, in the lifting up two elements, the earth element and the water element,
are subordinate and sluggish while the other two are predominant and strong.
vsm2.20:64.2: Likewise in the shifting forward and shifting sideways.
vsm2.20:64.3:
In the lowering down two elements, the fire element and the air element,
are subordinate and sluggish while the other two are predominant and strong.
vsm2.20:64.4: Likewise in the placing down and fixing down.
vsm2.20:64.5:
He attributes the three characteristics to materiality according to “disappearance of what grows
old in each stage” by means of these six parts into which he has thus divided it.
vsm2.20:65.2:
The elements and the kinds of derived materiality occurring in the lifting up all ceased there without
reaching the shifting forward: therefore they are impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:65.3:
Likewise those occurring in the shifting forward … the shifting sideways; those occurring in the shifting
sideways … the lowering down; those occurring in the lowering down … the placing down;
vsm2.20:65.4: those occurring in the placing down cease there without reaching the fixing down;
vsm2.20:65.5:
thus formations keep breaking up, like crackling sesame seeds put into a hot pan; wherever they arise,
there they cease stage by stage, section by section, term by term, each without reaching the next part:
vsm2.20:65.6: therefore they are impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:66.1: When he sees formations stage by stage with insight thus, his comprehension of materiality has become subtle.
vsm2.20:66.2: Here is a simile for its subtlety.
vsm2.20:66.3: A border dweller, it seems, who was familiar with torches of wood and grass, etc., but had never seen a lamp before, came to a city.
vsm2.20:66.4: Seeing a lamp burning in the market, he asked a man, “I say, what is that lovely thing called?”
vsm2.20:66.5: “What is lovely about that? It is called a lamp.
vsm2.20:66.6: Where it goes to when its oil and wick are used up no one knows.”
vsm2.20:66.7: Another told him, “That is crudely put; for the flame in each third portion of the wick as it gradually burns up
vsm2.20:66.8: ceases there without reaching the other parts.”
vsm2.20:66.9: Other told him, “That is crudely put too; for the flame in each inch, in each half-inch,
vsm2.20:66.10: in each thread, in each strand, will cease without reaching the other strands;
vsm2.20:66.11: but the flame cannot appear without a strand.”
vsm2.20:67.1:
Herein, the meditator’s attribution of the three characteristics to materiality delimited by the hundred years as “taking
up” and “putting down” is like the man’s knowledge stated thus, “Where it goes when its oil and wick are used up no one knows.”
vsm2.20:67.2:
The meditator’s attribution of the three characteristics according to “disappearance of what grows old in each
stage” to the materiality delimited by the third part of the hundred years is like the man’s knowledge stated thus,
“The flame in each third portion of the wick ceases without reaching the other parts.”
vsm2.20:67.3:
The meditator’s attribution of the three characteristics to materiality delimited by the periods of ten, five, four, three,
two years, one year, is like the man’s knowledge stated thus, “The flame in each inch will cease without reaching the others.”
vsm2.20:67.4:
The meditator’s attribution of the three characteristics to materiality delimited by the four-month and two-month
periods by classing the year as threefold and sixfold respectively according to the seasons is like the man’s
knowledge stated thus, “The flame in each half-inch will cease without reaching the others.”
vsm2.20:67.5:
The meditator’s attribution of the three characteristics to materiality delimited by means of the dark and bright
halves of the moon, by means of night and day, and by means of morning, etc., taking one night and day in six parts,
is like the man’s knowledge stated thus, “The flame in each thread will cease without reaching the others.”
vsm2.20:67.6:
The meditator’s attribution of the three characteristics to materiality delimited by means of each part,
namely, “moving forward,” etc., and “lifting up,” etc., is like the man’s knowledge stated thus,
“The flame in each strand will cease without reaching the others.”
vsm2.20:68.1:
Having in various ways thus attributed the three characteristics to materiality
according to “disappearance of what grows old in each stage,” he analyzes that same materiality
vsm2.20:68.2:
and divides it into four portions as “arising from nutriment,” etc., and he again
attributes the three characteristics to each portion.
vsm2.20:68.3: Herein, materiality arising from nutriment becomes evident to him through hunger and its satisfaction.
vsm2.20:68.4:
For materiality that is originated when one is hungry is parched and stale, and it
is as ugly and disfigured as a parched stump, as a crow perching in a charcoal pit.
vsm2.20:68.5: That originated when hunger is satisfied is plump, fresh, tender, smooth and soft to touch.
vsm2.20:68.6: Discerning that, he attributes the three characteristics to it thus:
vsm2.20:68.7:
The materiality occurring when hunger is satisfied ceases there without reaching the time
when one is hungry; therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:69.1: That arising from temperature becomes evident through cool and heat.
vsm2.20:69.2: For materiality that is originated when it is hot is parched, stale and ugly.
vsm2.20:69.3: Materiality originated by cool temperature is plump, fresh, tender, smooth, and soft to touch.
vsm2.20:69.4:
Discerning that, he attributes the three characteristics to it thus: The materiality occurring
when it is hot ceases there without reaching the time when it is cool.
vsm2.20:69.5:
The materiality occurring when it is cool ceases there without reaching the time when it is hot:
therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:70.1: The kamma-born becomes evident through the sense doors, that is, the base of consciousness.
vsm2.20:70.2:
For in the case of the eye door there are thirty material instances with decads of the eye,
the body, and sex; but with the twenty-four instances originated by temperature, consciousness, and nutriment,
that is to say, three bare octads, which are their support, there are fifty-four.
vsm2.20:70.3: Likewise in the case of the doors of the ear, nose, and tongue.
vsm2.20:70.4:
In the case of the body door there are forty-four with the decads of body and sex and the instances
originated by temperature, and so on.
vsm2.20:70.5:
In the case of the mind door there are fifty-four, too, with the decads of the heart-basis,
the body, and sex, and those instances originated by the temperature, and so on.
vsm2.20:70.6:
Discerning all that materiality, he attributes the three characteristics to it thus:
The materiality occurring in the eye door ceases there without reaching the ear door;
vsm2.20:70.7:
the materiality occurring in the ear door … the nose door; the materiality occurring in the nose door
… the tongue door; the materiality occurring in the tongue door … the body door;
vsm2.20:70.8:
the materiality occurring in the body door ceases there without reaching the mind door:
therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:71.1: The consciousness-originated becomes evident through the behaviour of one who is joyful or grieved.
vsm2.20:71.2: For the materiality arisen at the time when he is joyful is smooth, tender, fresh and soft to touch.
vsm2.20:71.3: That arisen at the time when he is grieved is parched, stale and ugly.
vsm2.20:71.4:
Discerning that, he attributes the three characteristics to it thus: The materiality occurring at the time
when one is joyful ceases there without reaching the time when one is grieved;
vsm2.20:71.5:
the materiality occurring at the time when one is grieved ceases there without reaching the time
when one is joyful: therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:72.1:
When he discerns consciousness-originated materiality and attributes the three
characteristics to it in this way, this meaning becomes evident to him:
vsm2.20:72.2:
> Life, person, pleasure, pain just these alone
> Join in one conscious moment that flicks by.
> Gods, though they live for four-and-eighty thousand
> Eons, are not the same for two such moments. > Ceased aggregates of those dead or alive
> Are all alike, gone never to return;
> And those that break up meanwhile, and in future,
> Have traits no different from those ceased before.

> No world is born if consciousness is not
> Produced; when that is present, then it lives;
> When consciousness dissolves, the world is dead:
> The highest sense this concept will allow.

> No store of broken states, no future stock;
> Those born balance like seeds on needle points.
> Breakup of states is foredoomed at their birth;
> Those present decay, unmingled with those past.
> They come from nowhere, break up, nowhere go;
> Flash in and out, as lightning in the sky (Nidd I 42).
vsm2.20:73.1:
Having attributed the three characteristics to that arising from nutriment, etc.,
he again attributes the three characteristics to natural materiality.
vsm2.20:73.2:
Natural materiality is a name for external materiality that is not bound up with faculties and arises
along with the eon of world expansion, for example, iron, copper, tin, lead, gold, silver, pearl, gem, beryl,
conch shell, marble, coral, ruby, opal, soil, stone, rock, grass, tree, creeper, and so on (see Vibh 83).
vsm2.20:73.3: That becomes evident to him by means of an asoka-tree shoot.
vsm2.20:74.1: For that to begin with is pale pink;
vsm2.20:74.2: then in two or three days it becomes dense red,
vsm2.20:74.3: again in two or three days it becomes dull red,
vsm2.20:74.4: next brown, the colour of a tender mango shoot;
vsm2.20:74.5: next, the colour of a growing shoot;
vsm2.20:74.6: next, the colour of pale leaves; next, the colour of dark green leaves.
vsm2.20:74.7:
After it has become the colour of dark green leaves, as it follows out the successive stages of such material continuity,
it eventually becomes withered foliage, and at the end of the year it breaks loose from its stem and falls off.
vsm2.20:75.1:
Discerning that, he attributes the three characteristics to it thus: The materiality occurring when
it is pale pink ceases there without reaching the time when it is dense red;
vsm2.20:75.2: the materiality occurring when it is dense red … dull red;
vsm2.20:75.3: the materiality occurring when it is dull red … the colour of a tender mango shoot;
vsm2.20:75.4: the materiality occurring when it is the colour of a tender mango shoot … the colour of a growing shoot;
vsm2.20:75.5: the materiality occurring when it is the colour of a growing shoot … the colour of pale green leaves;
vsm2.20:75.6: the materiality occurring when it is the colour of pale green leaves … the colour of dark green leaves;
vsm2.20:75.7: the materiality occurring when it is the colour of dark green leaves … the time when it is withered foliage;
vsm2.20:75.8:
the materiality occurring when it is withered foliage ceases there without reaching the time when it
breaks loose from its stem and falls off: therefore it is impermanent, painful, not-self.
vsm2.20:75.9: He comprehends all natural materiality in this way.
vsm2.20:75.10: This is how, firstly, he comprehends formations by attributing the three characteristics to them by means of the material septad.
